content: # Network Incident Response Procedures
This document defines the standard procedures for responding to network incidents across all SmartConnect regions. Follow these steps to ensure consistent and timely resolution.

### Critical (P1)

Network-wide outage or complete service disruption affecting more than 10,000 customers. Examples include backbone fiber cuts, core router failures, or DNS infrastructure collapse. Response time must be within 15 minutes of detection. Escalation to VP of Network Operations is mandatory.

### High (P2)

Partial outage affecting a single region or technology tier. Up to 10,000 customers impacted. Examples include regional base station cluster failures, BNG (Broadband Network Gateway) overloads, or LTE core failures. Response time must be within 30 minutes.

### Medium (P3)

Degraded service in a limited area affecting fewer than 2,000 customers. Examples include individual cell site capacity overloads, backhaul congestion, or intermittent connectivity issues. Response time must be within 2 hours.

### Low (P4)

Minor performance degradation affecting fewer than 500 customers. Examples include elevated latency, minor packet loss, or non-critical service degradation. Response time must be within 8 hours.

### Step 1: Verify the Alert

Confirm the alert is valid by checking network monitoring dashboards. Cross-reference with customer trouble reports. Check if a maintenance window is active. Determine if the issue is localized or widespread.

### Step 2: Notify stakeholders

Send notification to the Network Operations Center (NOC) team lead. Update the incident bridge channel. If P1 or P2, notify regional operations managers. Log initial assessment in the incident management system.

### Step 3: Gather diagnostic data

Collect relevant logs from affected network elements. Capture interface statistics and error counters. Record routing table state. Note any recent configuration changes. Preserve packet captures if available.

### Step 4: Identify root cause

Analyze collected data to determine root cause. Check for correlation with known issues. Review change management records for recent modifications. Consult vendor documentation if hardware-related. Document findings in real-time.

### Tier 1: NOC Team

Handles P3 and P4 incidents. Performs initial triage and basic troubleshooting. Escalates to Tier 2 if not resolved within 2 hours.

### Tier 2: Regional Engineers

Handles P2 incidents and escalated P3 incidents. Performs advanced troubleshooting. Coordinates with vendors if needed. Escalates to Tier 3 if not resolved within 4 hours.

### Tier 3: Network Architects

Handles P1 incidents and escalated P2 incidents. Coordinates cross-functional response. Makes architecture-level decisions. Engages vendor support at highest priority.

### Tier 4: Vendor Support

Engaged for hardware failures or complex software issues. Provides TAC (Technical Assistance Center) support. Coordinates RMA (Return Merchandise Authorization) for defective equipment.

### Initial Notification

Incident detected: [severity] - [description] - [affected region] - [estimated customers impacted] - [investigation status]

### Resolution Update

Incident resolved: [incident_id] - [root cause] - [resolution] - [duration] - [preventive measures]

All P1 and P2 incidents require a post-incident review within 48 hours. The review must include timeline, root cause analysis, customer impact assessment, and preventive action items. Results are shared with the Operations team and logged in the knowledge base.

### Network Recovery

Verify all affected sites are operational. Confirm routing convergence. Validate customer connectivity through synthetic tests. Monitor for 30 minutes post-recovery to ensure stability.

### Customer Recovery

Notify affected customers of service restoration. Provide credits if SLA was breached. Update ticket status and close related support tickets. Send satisfaction survey after 48 hours.
# Network Health Monitoring Standards
This document defines the monitoring standards used to assess network health across SmartConnect infrastructure. All monitoring follows the three-state model: Healthy, Degraded, and Critical.

### Healthy

All network sites in the monitored group are operational with no active events. No alarms with severity higher than informational are present. Key performance indicators are within normal thresholds.

### Degraded

One or more sites are in maintenance mode or have active non-critical events. Performance metrics are elevated but service is available. Customer impact is limited or non-existent.

### Critical

One or more sites are offline. Active critical or high-severity events are present. Service is disrupted or significantly degraded. Customer-facing services are affected.

The network health status is calculated using the following deterministic rules:

1. If any sites in the monitored set have status "offline", the health is "critical".
2. If any sites have active events with event_type "maintenance" or "degradation", the health is "degraded".
3. Otherwise, the health is "healthy".

These rules are applied in priority order. Critical status overrides degraded, which overrides healthy.

### GET /api/network/health

Returns aggregated network health for all sites or filtered by region. Response includes total sites, operational count, degraded count, maintenance count, offline count, overall status, and active event count.

### GET /api/network/sites

Returns individual site status with health indicators. Each site includes its current operational state, capacity utilization, and last maintenance timestamp.

### Site Availability

Measured as percentage of time a site is operational in a 24-hour window. Target is 99.9% for Tier 1 sites, 99.5% for Tier 2 sites, and 99.0% for Tier 3 sites.

### Capacity Utilization

Current utilization as percentage of total capacity. Thresholds: below 60% is normal, 60-80% is elevated, 80-95% is high, above 95% is critical.

### Event Rate

Number of active events per site. More than 3 active events per site triggers a review. More than 5 active events per site triggers automatic escalation.

### Response Time

Average round-trip time for synthetic probes. Baseline is established during the first 7 days of monitoring. Deviations greater than 50% from baseline trigger alerts.

### Immediate Alert (P1)

Site offline for more than 5 minutes. More than 500 customers affected. Backbone link failure. Core router interface down.

### Urgent Alert (P2)

Site degraded for more than 15 minutes. Capacity above 90%. Error rate above 0.1%. BNG session count above 80% capacity.

### Warning (P3)

Site in maintenance for more than 4 hours. Capacity above 75%. Error rate above 0.01%. Backhaul utilization above 70%.

### Informational (P4)

Scheduled maintenance starting. Capacity above 60%. Minor configuration change applied. Software update completed.

The monitoring data feeds into the Operations Overview dashboard. Key metrics displayed include network health status, site status counts, active events, and regional health breakdown. All metrics update in real-time through the API layer.

For enterprise customers, additional SLA-specific monitoring applies. Network availability must meet the terms specified in the customer's service level agreement. Breach of SLA thresholds triggers automatic escalation and customer notification.
# Cell Site Operations Guide

### Macro Sites

Full-size cell towers providing wide area coverage. Typically mounted on dedicated towers or building rooftops. Equipment includes baseband units, remote radio heads, antennas, and backhaul equipment. Macro sites serve the highest number of users and carry the most traffic.

### Small Cells

Low-power base stations for capacity injection in high-density areas. Mounted on street furniture, utility poles, or building facades. Used to fill coverage gaps and boost capacity in urban cores. Typically connect via fiber or microwave backhaul.

### Distributed Antenna Systems (DAS)

Network of antennas distributed throughout a building or venue. Used for indoor coverage in large facilities such as airports, stadiums, and convention centers. Connected to a central base station via fiber or coaxial cable.

### Operational

Site is fully functional and serving customers. All equipment is powered and connected. No active alarms above informational level.

### Degraded

Site is operational but experiencing issues. May have reduced capacity, single-carrier operation, or minor equipment faults. Customers may experience degraded service quality.

### Maintenance

Site is undergoing planned work. May be partially or fully out of service during maintenance window. Customers should be notified before scheduled maintenance.

### Offline

Site is not operational. No service is being provided. Customers in the coverage area are affected. Immediate investigation is required.

### Normal Utilization (0-60%)

Site is operating well within capacity. No action required. Continue monitoring.

### Elevated Utilization (60-80%)

Site is approaching capacity limits. Schedule capacity upgrade assessment. Consider adding carriers or upgrading hardware. Monitor for further increases.

### High Utilization (80-95%)

Site is near maximum capacity. Initiate capacity expansion project. Implement traffic management policies. Consider temporary solutions such as COW (Cell on Wheels).

### Critical Utilization (95%+)

Site is at or beyond capacity. Immediate capacity injection required. Implement emergency traffic management. Prioritize voice over data if necessary.

### Fiber Backhaul

Preferred for high-capacity sites. Minimum 1 Gbps for macro sites, 100 Mbps for small cells. Redundant paths required for Tier 1 sites. Latency must be below 5ms.

### Microwave Backhaul

Used where fiber is not available. Minimum 200 Mbps for macro sites. Dual diversity required for reliable operation. Frequency coordination needed to avoid interference.

### Satellite Backhaul

Used for remote sites only. Minimum 50 Mbps. High latency (600ms+) is expected. Used as temporary solution while fiber or microwave is deployed.

### Preventive Maintenance

Quarterly inspection of all sites. Includes physical inspection, equipment testing, firmware updates, and cleaning. Battery backup testing monthly. Generator testing quarterly for sites with backup power.

### Corrective Maintenance

Response based on site tier. Tier 1 sites: 4-hour response, 8-hour repair. Tier 2 sites: 8-hour response, 24-hour repair. Tier 3 sites: 24-hour response, 48-hour repair.

### No Service from Site

Verify power supply is active. Check backhaul connectivity. Verify base station software is running. Check for alarms on management system. Verify antenna connections. Test with portable equipment if available.

### Intermittent Service

Check for interference sources near the site. Verify antenna alignment and physical condition. Check for loose connections. Review error logs for patterns. Monitor during different times of day.

### Capacity Issues

Review traffic patterns and growth trends. Identify peak usage hours. Check for failed or degraded carriers. Consider adding carriers or upgrading to higher capacity hardware.
# Network Technology Overview

Long Term Evolution provides high-speed wireless broadband. Supports peak speeds up to 150 Mbps downlink and 50 Mbps uplink. Used for mobile broadband, IoT, and voice over LTE (VoLTE). Coverage is provided by macro and small cell sites across all regions.

### LTE Coverage Bands

Band 2 (1900 MHz): Primary coverage band for urban and suburban areas. Good balance of coverage and capacity.

Band 4 (1700/2100 MHz): AWS band used for capacity in urban areas. Higher capacity but shorter range.

Band 12 (700 MHz): Low-band for rural coverage and building penetration. Longer range but lower capacity.

Band 66 (1700/2100 MHz): Extended AWS band for additional capacity.

New Radio provides next-generation wireless connectivity. Supports peak speeds up to 10 Gbps downlink. Used for enhanced mobile broadband, ultra-reliable low-latency communications, and massive machine-type communications.

### 5G Deployment Modes

#### Non-Standalone (NSA)

5G NR deployed on top of existing LTE core. Provides increased capacity and speed without new core infrastructure. Uses EN-DC (EUTRA-NR Dual Connectivity) for device connection.

#### Standalone (SA)

Full 5G NR with 5G core. Enables all 5G features including network slicing and ultra-low latency. Deployed in select urban areas.

### 5G Frequency Bands

n71 (600 MHz): Low-band 5G for wide coverage. Good building penetration but limited capacity.

n41 (2500 MHz): Mid-band 5G for balanced coverage and capacity. Primary 5G band for urban areas.

n260 (39 GHz): mmWave 5G for ultra-high capacity in dense areas. Limited range and poor building penetration.

UMTS/HSPA technology providing basic mobile broadband. Supports peak speeds up to 42 Mbps downlink. Being phased out in favor of 4G and 5G. Still operational in some rural areas for backward compatibility.

### Radio Access Network (RAN)

Base stations (eNodeB for LTE, gNodeB for 5G) provide wireless access. Connected to the core network via backhaul. Includes baseband processing, radio transmission, and antenna systems.

### Core Network

Centralized network functions including mobility management, session management, and subscriber management. Evolved Packet Core (EPC) for LTE. 5G Core (5GC) for 5G SA.

### Transport Network

Interconnects RAN and core network. Includes backhaul (site to aggregation), midhaul (aggregation to core), and fronthaul (baseband to radio). Fiber, microwave, and Ethernet are primary transport technologies.

### VoLTE (Voice over LTE)

IP-based voice service on LTE. Provides HD voice quality. Supports simultaneous voice and data. Required for voice service as 3G is retired.

### VoNR (Voice over New Radio)

IP-based voice service on 5G SA. Provides even lower latency and higher quality. Used in 5G standalone deployments.

### VoWiFi (Voice over Wi-Fi)

Voice service over Wi-Fi networks. Used for indoor coverage and areas with poor cellular coverage. Seamless handoff between Wi-Fi and cellular.

### NB-IoT (Narrowband IoT)

Low-power wide-area technology for IoT devices. Supports deep indoor coverage. Used for smart metering, asset tracking, and environmental monitoring.

### LTE-M (Cat-M1)

Medium-power IoT technology. Supports mobility and handover. Used for connected vehicles, wearable devices, and industrial IoT.
# Spectrum Management and Allocation

This document describes how SmartConnect manages and allocates wireless spectrum across its network. Spectrum is a finite resource that must be carefully managed to ensure optimal network performance.

### Low-Band Spectrum (600-900 MHz)

Provides wide area coverage and excellent building penetration. Used primarily for rural coverage and indoor penetration in urban areas. Includes 600 MHz (n71/71), 700 MHz (B12), and 850 MHz bands. These bands carry voice and low-bandwidth data services.

### Mid-Band Spectrum (1.7-3.7 GHz)

Provides balanced coverage and capacity. Primary bands for urban and suburban capacity. Includes 1700/2100 MHz (B4/B66), 1900 MHz (B2), and 2500 MHz (B41/n41) bands. These bands carry the majority of mobile broadband traffic.

### High-Band Spectrum (24-39 GHz)

Provides ultra-high capacity in dense areas. Limited range and building penetration. Used for hotspots, venues, and dense urban cores. Includes 28 GHz and 39 GHz (n260) bands. These bands support peak data rates.

### Voice Priority

Voice services always receive priority allocation during congestion. VoLTE and VoNR calls are allocated dedicated bearers with guaranteed bit rates. Voice traffic cannot be deprioritized or throttled.

### Data Traffic Management

Best-effort data traffic is managed using quality of service (QoS) classes. Streaming video is allocated medium priority. Web browsing is allocated standard priority. File downloads and backups are allocated low priority.

### IoT Allocation

IoT devices are allocated narrow bandwidth channels. NB-IoT uses 180 kHz channels. LTE-M uses 1.4 MHz channels. These allocations are isolated from consumer traffic.

### External Interference

Caused by non-network sources such as illegal transmitters, faulty electronics, or adjacent systems. Detected through spectrum monitoring and customer reports. Resolution involves coordination with regulatory authorities.

### Internal Interference

Caused by network elements such as adjacent cells or overlapping frequencies. Managed through frequency planning and power control. Coordinated multipoint (CoMP) techniques reduce inter-cell interference.

Combines multiple frequency carriers to increase bandwidth. Up to 5 carriers can be aggregated in LTE. Up to 16 carriers in 5G NR. Carrier aggregation is dynamically adjusted based on network load and device capabilities.

Allows simultaneous operation of LTE and 5G NR on the same frequency band. Resources are allocated based on demand. Enables smooth transition from 4G to 5G without requiring separate spectrum allocations.
# Mobile Data Connectivity Troubleshooting

### No Data Connection

Device shows signal bars but cannot access internet. Web pages fail to load. Applications cannot connect. Speed test shows 0 Mbps or fails entirely.

### Slow Data

Pages load slowly. Video buffers frequently. Applications time out. Speed test shows significantly lower than expected speeds.

### Intermittent Data

Connection drops periodically. Applications disconnect and reconnect. Downloads fail partway through. Web pages partially load.

### Step 1: Check Device Status

Verify mobile data is enabled in device settings. Check that airplane mode is off. Confirm SIM card is active and not locked. Verify APN settings are correct.

### Step 2: Check Network Coverage

Check coverage map for the user's location. Verify the site serving the user is operational. Check for active network events in the area. Confirm the user's subscription includes data service.

### Step 3: Run Speed Test

Use the network speed test tool. Record download and upload speeds. Note latency and jitter values. Compare against plan expectations.

### Step 4: Check for Congestion

Review site capacity utilization. Check time of day for peak usage. Look for recent traffic spikes. Verify no maintenance is in progress.

### APN Configuration Issues

If APN settings are incorrect, guide the user through resetting APN to default. For Android: Settings > Mobile Networks > Access Point Names > Reset to default. For iOS: Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > Reset Settings. After reset, reboot the device.

### SIM Card Issues

If SIM shows as invalid, try reseating the SIM card. If SIM is locked, guide user through PUK code entry. If SIM is damaged, arrange replacement. If SIM is suspended, verify account status.

### Network Registration Issues

If device is not registered on the network, toggle airplane mode on and off. If persistent, manually select network operator. If still unresolved, check for SIM provisioning issues.

### Speed Issues

If speed is low despite good signal, check for background app data usage. Verify no VPN is active. Check for data throttling due to plan limits. Test at different times to rule out congestion.

### Signal Quality Analysis

Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP): Above -80 dBm is excellent, -80 to -90 dBm is good, -90 to -100 dBm is fair, below -100 dBm is poor.

Reference Signal Received Quality (RSRQ): Above -10 dB is excellent, -10 to -15 dB is good, -15 to -20 dB is fair, below -20 dB is poor.

Signal to Interference plus Noise Ratio (SINR): Above 20 dB is excellent, 13-20 dB is good, 0-13 dB is fair, below 0 dB is poor.

### Handover Issues

Check for frequent handovers between cells. Review handover failure rates. Check for ping-pong handovers between overlapping cells. Verify handover parameters are optimized.

Escalate to Tier 2 support if: issue persists after all standard troubleshooting, device is not compatible with network bands, multiple users in same area report similar issues, or issue requires network-side investigation.
# Wi-Fi Calling Setup and Troubleshooting

Wi-Fi Calling (VoWiFi) allows customers to make and receive calls over Wi-Fi networks when cellular coverage is poor or unavailable. This service uses the customer's existing phone number and plan minutes.

### Device Requirements

Device must support Wi-Fi Calling. Most modern smartphones support this feature. Check device specifications for compatibility. Device software must be up to date.

### Account Requirements

Customer must have an active postpaid account. Wi-Fi Calling must be enabled on the account. Customer must have a compatible device. SIM card must be provisioned for Wi-Fi Calling.

### Network Requirements

Device needs a working Wi-Fi internet connection. Minimum 1 Mbps for HD voice calls. Minimum 2 Mbps for video calls. Stable connection with low packet loss.

### Android Devices

1. Open Settings on the device.
2. Navigate to Connections or Network & Internet.
3. Select Wi-Fi Calling.
4. Toggle Wi-Fi Calling to On.
5. Select calling preference: Wi-Fi Preferred or Cellular Preferred.
6. Complete any additional prompts.

### iOS Devices

1. Open Settings on the device.
2. Navigate to Phone or Cellular.
3. Select Wi-Fi Calling.
4. Toggle Wi-Fi Calling to On.
5. Confirm the emergency address when prompted.
6. Complete any additional prompts.

### Emergency Address Registration

Wi-Fi Calling requires a registered emergency address for E911 services. During setup, device will prompt for emergency address. Enter the primary address where the device will be used. Verify the address is correct. Update if address changes.

### Wi-Fi Calling Not Available

Verify Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on the account. Check device compatibility. Ensure device software is up to date. Verify SIM card is active. Restart device and try again.

### Calls Not Connecting Over Wi-Fi

Check Wi-Fi internet connection is working. Verify Wi-Fi Calling is enabled in device settings. Check for firewall or port blocking on the Wi-Fi network. Required ports: UDP 500, UDP 4500, and IP protocol 50.

### Poor Call Quality on Wi-Fi

Check Wi-Fi signal strength. Minimum 2 bars recommended. Verify internet connection speed meets requirements. Reduce number of devices on the Wi-Fi network. Move closer to the Wi-Fi router. Consider using 5 GHz Wi-Fi band instead of 2.4 GHz.

### Calls Dropping When Switching Between Wi-Fi and Cellular

This is normal behavior during initial setup. Seamless handoff improves after a few calls. Ensure both Wi-Fi Calling and cellular are enabled. Check device settings for handover preferences. Update device software if issue persists.

Wi-Fi Calling does not support premium SMS services. Some carrier-specific features may not be available over Wi-Fi. Emergency calls may use the registered Wi-Fi Calling address rather than current location. Video calling over Wi-Fi may have lower quality than over cellular.
# APN Configuration Guide

Access Point Name (APN) is the gateway between the mobile network and the internet. It determines the network path for all data traffic. Correct APN configuration is essential for mobile data to function.

### SmartConnect Internet APN

APN: smartconnect.internet  
Proxy: Not set  
Port: Not set  
Username: Not set  
Password: Not set  
Server: Not set  
MMSC: Not set

MMS Port: Not set  
MCC: 310  
MNC: 260

### SmartConnect MMS APN

Name: SmartConnect MMS  
APN: smartconnect.mms  
Proxy: Not set  
Port: Not set  
Username: Not set

MMSC: http://mmsc.smartconnect.com

### Android Configuration

1. Open Settings.
2. Navigate to Mobile Networks > Access Point Names.
3. Tap the menu icon and select New APN.
4. Enter the APN settings as listed above.
5. Save the new APN.
6. Select the new APN as the active APN.
7. Restart the device.

### iOS Configuration

iOS devices typically configure APN automatically through the carrier settings update. If manual configuration is needed:

1. Open Settings.
2. Navigate to Cellular > Cellular Data Options > Cellular Network.
3. Enter the APN settings under the Cellular Data section.
4. For MMS, enter the MMS settings under the MMS section.
5. Restart the device.

### Automatic Configuration

Most devices will automatically configure APN settings when a SmartConnect SIM is inserted. If data does not work after inserting the SIM, try: removing and reinserting the SIM, toggling airplane mode, or restarting the device. If automatic configuration fails, use manual configuration above.

### Data Not Working After APN Change

Verify the APN settings match the defaults exactly. Check for typos in the APN name or settings. Ensure the APN is selected as active. Restart the device after making changes. If issues persist, reset APN to defaults and reconfigure.

### MMS Not Working

Verify MMS APN is configured correctly. Check that mobile data is enabled. Verify the messaging app has necessary permissions. Check for sufficient storage space on the device. Test MMS by sending a picture message.

### Roaming Data Not Working

Verify roaming is enabled on the device. Check that roaming is enabled on the account. Verify the roaming APN settings. Some devices require manual APN configuration while roaming. Contact support if roaming data still does not work.
# Service Activation Procedures
This document describes the procedures for activating new services and modifying existing services for SmartConnect customers.

### Pre-Activation Checks

Verify customer identity and account status. Confirm the customer has a valid IMEI for the device they will use. Check that the desired phone number is available. Verify the selected plan is available for the customer's segment. Confirm the customer understands the service terms and pricing.

### Activation Steps

1. Create or locate the customer account in the billing system.
2. Select the desired plan and add it to the order.
3. Generate a new SIM card assignment or eSIM profile.
4. Associate the SIM with the customer account and selected plan.
5. Provision network access for the new subscription.
6. Configure the customer's device with the correct APN settings.
7. Verify service is working by placing a test call and using data.
8. Send welcome SMS and email with account details.

### Post-Activation Verification

Make a test call to verify voice service. Send a test SMS to verify messaging. Run a speed test to verify data service. Verify the customer can access their account portal. Confirm billing is set up correctly.

### Upgrade

Verify the customer's eligibility for the new plan. Check for any contract commitments that may be affected. Calculate any prorated charges for the current billing cycle. Apply the new plan effective immediately or at next billing cycle. Notify the customer of the change and new features.

### Downgrade

Verify the customer understands the features they will lose. Check for any minimum plan requirements. Calculate any prorated credits for the current billing cycle. Apply the new plan effective at next billing cycle unless customer requests immediate. Notify the customer of the change.

### Plan Migration

When discontinuing a plan, migrate affected customers to the closest equivalent plan. Notify customers at least 30 days before the migration. Provide comparison of old and new plan features. Offer promotional pricing if available. Assist with any device changes needed.

### New Device on Existing Line

Verify the new device IMEI is compatible with the network. Check for any device locks or blacklisting. Provision the new device on the customer's existing line. Transfer any service features to the new device. Verify all services work on the new device.

### SIM Swap

Verify the customer's identity before processing. Deactivate the old SIM immediately. Activate the new SIM with the same phone number and plan. Verify service is restored on the new SIM. The old SIM becomes permanently inactive.

### eSIM Activation

Verify the device supports eSIM. Generate an eSIM QR code for the customer. Guide the customer through scanning the QR code. Verify the eSIM is activated and service is working. Deactivate any physical SIM if being replaced.

### Voluntary Suspension

Customer requests temporary service suspension. Maximum suspension period is 90 days. A reduced monthly fee applies during suspension. All services are suspended including voice, data, and messaging. Service resumes automatically after the suspension period or upon customer request.

### Involuntary Suspension

Triggered by non-payment or policy violation. Customer is notified before suspension takes effect. Suspension occurs after the grace period expires. All services are suspended. Customer must resolve the issue to restore service.

Verify the issue causing suspension is resolved. Reactivate the subscription in the billing system. Provision network access for the subscription. Verify all services are working. Notify the customer that service has been restored. Apply any applicable restoration fees.
# Coverage Issue Resolution

### Good Coverage

RSRP above -90 dBm. RSRQ above -10 dB. SINR above 13 dB. Consistent signal without drops. Full speed data and reliable voice calls.

### Fair Coverage

RSRP between -90 and -105 dBm. RSRQ between -10 and -15 dB. SINR between 0 and 13 dB. Signal may vary. Data may be slower during peak hours. Voice calls generally work.

### Poor Coverage

RSRP below -105 dBm. RSRQ below -15 dB. SINR below 0 dB. Inconsistent signal. Frequent drops. Very slow data. Dropped calls likely.

### No Coverage

No detectable signal from any SmartConnect site. Device shows no service. No calls, texts, or data available.

### Indoor Coverage Gaps

Low-band spectrum (600-700 MHz) provides best indoor penetration. Mid-band spectrum (1.7-2.5 GHz) provides moderate indoor coverage. High-band spectrum (mmWave) has poor indoor penetration. Building materials affect signal penetration significantly.

Resolution: Recommend Wi-Fi Calling for persistent indoor issues. Check if the building has a DAS or small cell. Suggest a signal booster for single-location improvement. Report coverage gap for network planning.

### Rural Coverage Gaps

Low population density makes rural coverage expensive. Low-band spectrum provides the widest rural coverage. Satellite backhaul may limit rural site capacity. Terrain affects coverage significantly.

Resolution: Verify the customer is within the coverage area. Check for known coverage gaps in the area. Suggest alternative carrier options if SmartConnect does not cover the area. Log the coverage gap for network expansion planning.

### Outdoor Dead Zones

Dead zones can occur between cell sites. Terrain features like hills and valleys cause dead zones. Dense urban environments with tall buildings cause signal shadowing. Construction zones may temporarily affect coverage.

Resolution: Verify the exact location of the dead zone. Check if it is a known coverage gap. Report the dead zone for network investigation. Suggest workaround routes or locations for consistent service.

### Step 1: Verify the Issue

Confirm the customer is within the SmartConnect coverage area. Check the coverage map for the reported location. Verify the customer's device supports the required frequency bands. Check for active network events in the area.

### Step 2: Gather Information

Collect the exact location of the coverage issue. Determine if the issue is indoors or outdoors. Note the time of day and duration of the issue. Ask about surrounding buildings or terrain features. Collect device model and operating system information.

### Step 3: Check Network Status

Review the site serving the area for any active events. Check site capacity and utilization. Verify site configuration and antenna alignment. Check for recent changes to the site.

### Step 4: Escalate if Needed

If the issue is confirmed and not resolved by standard troubleshooting, escalate to network engineering. Provide all collected information including location, device details, and network status. The network team will investigate and plan resolution.

### Small Cell Deployment

Low-power base stations for targeted coverage improvement. Ideal for filling specific coverage gaps. Faster to deploy than macro sites. Used in urban areas for capacity and coverage.

### DAS Installation

Distributed antenna systems for large buildings and venues. Provides consistent indoor coverage. Requires coordination with building management. Used for airports, stadiums, and convention centers.

### Macro Site Construction

New tower sites for wide area coverage. Longest deployment timeline. Highest cost but provides comprehensive coverage. Used for new coverage areas and major capacity upgrades.
# Billing Cycle Management
This document describes how SmartConnect manages billing cycles, charges, and credits for customer accounts.

### Monthly Billing

Most plans are billed monthly on the anniversary of the service activation date. The billing cycle day is set at activation and remains consistent each month. Charges are prorated for the first and last month of service.

### Billing Cycle Day

The billing cycle day (BCD) is the day of the month when the bill is generated. This is determined by the customer's activation date. For example, if activated on the 15th, the BCD is the 15th of each month. The customer can request a BCD change, which may result in a short or long billing cycle.

### Bill Generation

Bills are generated on the BCD and include all charges for the billing period. Charges include recurring plan fees, usage charges, taxes, and fees. Credits and adjustments are applied before the final amount is calculated.

### First Month Proration

When a customer activates mid-cycle, the first month is prorated. The proration is based on the number of days remaining in the billing cycle. For example, if activated on the 20th and the cycle ends on the 30th, the customer is charged for 11 days.

### Last Month Proration

When a customer deactivates mid-cycle, the final month is prorated. The proration is based on the number of days the service was active in the billing cycle. Any unused portion of the billing cycle is credited.

### Plan Change Proration

When a customer changes plans mid-cycle, charges are prorated. The old plan is prorated for the days it was active. The new plan is prorated for the remaining days. The difference is charged or credited accordingly.

### Service Credits

Credits for service disruptions or quality issues. Must be approved by a supervisor. Applied to the customer's next bill. Documented with a reason code and description.

### Goodwill Credits

Credits offered as a gesture of goodwill. Typically for customer retention or complaint resolution. Must be approved by a supervisor. Applied to the customer's next bill.

### Promotional Credits

Credits from promotional offers or discounts. Applied automatically based on the promotion terms. May be recurring or one-time. Expire at the end of the promotional period.

### Late Payment Fee

A late payment fee is charged if payment is not received by the due date. The fee is a percentage of the outstanding balance. The fee is capped at a maximum amount per billing cycle. Customers are notified before the late fee is applied.

### Grace Period

A grace period of 10 days is provided after the bill due date. No late fees are charged during the grace period. Service is not affected during the grace period. After the grace period, late fees are applied and service may be suspended.

### Non-Payment Suspension

If payment is not received within 30 days of the due date, service may be suspended. The customer is notified before suspension. All services including voice, data, and messaging are suspended. The customer must pay the outstanding balance plus any reconnection fees to restore service.

### Voluntary Cancellation Refund

Customers who cancel within the first 14 days receive a full refund minus any usage charges. Customers who cancel after 14 days receive a prorated refund for the unused portion of the current billing cycle. Any device subsidies or promotional balances become due immediately upon cancellation.

### Involuntary Termination Refund

Customers whose service is terminated due to non-payment do not receive a refund. Any device financing balances become due immediately. The account may be sent to collections if the balance remains unpaid.
# Data Usage and Throttling Policies

### Basic Plan

Includes 5 GB of high-speed data per month. After the data limit is reached, data speeds are reduced to 128 Kbps for the remainder of the billing cycle. The reduced speed applies to all data usage. The data limit resets at the beginning of the next billing cycle.

### Standard Plan

Includes 15 GB of high-speed data per month. After the data limit is reached, data speeds are reduced to 256 Kbps for the remainder of the billing cycle. The reduced speed applies to all data usage. The data limit resets at the beginning of the next billing cycle.

### Premium Plan

Includes 50 GB of high-speed data per month. After the data limit is reached, data speeds are reduced to 512 Kbps for the remainder of the billing cycle. The reduced speed applies to all data usage. The data limit resets at the beginning of the next billing cycle.

### Unlimited Plan

Includes unlimited high-speed data with no throttling. Subject to fair use policy. May be deprioritized during network congestion after 100 GB of usage. Deprioritization is temporary and based on network conditions.

### Speed Reduction

When a customer reaches their data limit, speed is reduced to the plan's throttled rate. The throttled rate is applied to all data traffic. No data is blocked, only slowed. The customer remains connected at the reduced speed.

### Data Usage Tracking

Data usage is tracked in real-time. Usage is recorded in 1 KB increments. The customer can check their current usage via the mobile app or customer portal. Usage updates may have a delay of up to 15 minutes.

### Throttle Removal

Speed restrictions are removed at the start of the next billing cycle. No action is required by the customer. The transition is automatic. If the customer upgrades their plan mid-cycle, the new plan's data limit applies immediately.

### Pay-Per-Use Overage

Customers on plans with data limits can opt for pay-per-use overage. Overage is charged at $10 per additional GB. Overage charges are capped at $50 per billing cycle. The cap does not include the base plan charge.

### Data Top-Up

Customers can purchase additional high-speed data at any time. Data top-up is available in 1 GB increments. Each 1 GB top-up costs $10. Top-up data does not roll over to the next billing cycle.

### Mobile App

Customers can check data usage through the SmartConnect mobile app. Real-time usage is displayed on the home screen. Historical usage charts show daily and monthly trends. Alerts can be configured for usage thresholds.

### Customer Portal

The web-based customer portal provides detailed usage information. Usage can be broken down by application type. Daily usage summaries are available. Usage alerts can be configured via email or SMS.

### Usage Alerts

Automatic alerts are sent at 50%, 75%, 90%, and 100% of the data limit. Alerts are sent via SMS and push notification. Additional custom alerts can be configured. Alerts are free and do not count against data usage.

### Dedicated Bandwidth

Enterprise plans include dedicated bandwidth with guaranteed minimum speeds. No throttling is applied to enterprise plans. Bandwidth is reserved for the customer's exclusive use. Upgrades and downgrades are managed through the account manager.

### Burst Capacity

Enterprise plans include burst capacity above the guaranteed bandwidth. Burst capacity is available during off-peak hours. Peak hours are defined as 8 AM to 8 PM local time. Burst capacity is not guaranteed and depends on network availability.
# Invoice Dispute Procedures
This document describes how SmartConnect handles disputes regarding invoice charges, billing errors, and service credits.

### Billing Error

The customer believes there is an error on their invoice. Examples include incorrect charges, missing credits, wrong plan pricing, or duplicate charges. Billing errors must be investigated and resolved within 30 days of the dispute.

### Service Quality

The customer experienced service quality issues and requests a credit. Examples include dropped calls, slow data, or service outages. Service quality credits require verification of the reported issue.

### Unauthorized Charges

The customer did not authorize or recognize a charge on their invoice. Examples include third-party charges, premium SMS, or subscription services. Unauthorized charges require investigation and may involve third-party coordination.

### Contract Dispute

The customer disagrees with contract terms or early termination fees. Examples include device financing, promotional commitments, or service agreements. Contract disputes are reviewed by the customer relations team.

### Step 1: Customer Contact

The customer contacts SmartConnect to initiate a dispute. The dispute can be initiated via phone, email, chat, or in-store visit. The customer provides their account number, invoice number, and description of the dispute. A dispute case number is generated and provided to the customer.

### Step 2: Initial Review

The customer service representative reviews the dispute during the initial contact. If the dispute can be resolved immediately, the representative applies the appropriate credit or adjustment. If the dispute requires investigation, it is escalated to the billing investigation team.

### Step 3: Investigation

The billing investigation team reviews all relevant information. This includes account history, usage records, service logs, and any supporting documentation provided by the customer. The investigation is completed within 10 business days for standard disputes and 30 business days for complex disputes.

### Step 4: Resolution

The investigation team determines the appropriate resolution. If the dispute is valid, a credit or adjustment is applied to the customer's account. If the dispute is not valid, the customer is notified with an explanation. The customer may appeal the decision if they disagree with the outcome.

### Step 5: Customer Notification

The customer is notified of the resolution via their preferred communication method. The notification includes a summary of the investigation, the determination, and any credits or adjustments applied. The customer's invoice is updated to reflect the resolution.

### Automatic Credits

Credits below $25 can be applied by customer service representatives without supervisor approval. Credits between $25 and $100 require supervisor approval. Credits above $100 require management approval. All credits are documented with a reason code.

### Recurring Credits

Recurring credits for ongoing issues are limited to 3 billing cycles. After 3 cycles, the issue must be escalated for permanent resolution. Recurring credits must be reviewed monthly to ensure they are still appropriate.

### Dispute Filing Deadline

Customers must file disputes within 60 days of the invoice date. Disputes filed after 60 days may not be eligible for credit. Exceptions are made for circumstances beyond the customer's control.

### Resolution Deadline

Standard disputes must be resolved within 30 business days. Complex disputes involving third parties may take up to 60 business days. Customers are notified of any delays and provided with an updated timeline.

### Appeal Deadline

Customers must file appeals within 30 days of the initial resolution. Appeals are reviewed by a different team than the initial investigation. The appeal decision is final and binding.

# Roaming Policies and Procedures

SmartConnect provides domestic and international roaming services to customers traveling outside their home coverage area. This document describes the policies, procedures, and troubleshooting for roaming services.

### What is Domestic Roaming

Domestic roaming occurs when a SmartConnect customer connects to another carrier's network within the country. This happens when the customer is outside SmartConnect's coverage area but within a roaming partner's coverage area. Roaming is automatic and requires no customer action.

### Domestic Roaming Charges

Domestic roaming is included at no additional cost for all postpaid plans. Data usage while roaming counts toward the customer's plan data limit. Voice and SMS usage while roaming is included in the plan allowances. There are no separate roaming fees for domestic roaming.

### Domestic Roaming Troubleshooting

If a customer cannot connect to a roaming network: verify roaming is enabled on the account, check that the customer is outside the SmartConnect coverage area, verify the device supports the roaming partner's frequency bands, and restart the device to force network reselection.

### International Roaming Plans

SmartConnect offers international roaming plans for customers traveling abroad. Plans are available in daily, weekly, and monthly options. Each plan includes a set amount of data, voice minutes, and SMS. Plans can be activated before departure or while abroad.

### International Roaming Charges

Without an international roaming plan, pay-per-use rates apply. Pay-per-use data is charged at $2.00 per MB. Pay-per-use voice calls are charged at $2.00 per minute for outgoing calls. Incoming calls are charged at $0.50 per minute. SMS is charged at $0.10 per message.

### International Roaming Activation

Customers must request international roaming activation before traveling. Activation can be done via the mobile app, customer portal, or by contacting customer service. A security deposit may be required for high-risk destinations. Activation takes effect within 24 hours.

### Partner Selection

The device automatically selects the best available roaming partner based on signal strength and quality. SmartConnect maintains roaming agreements with major carriers in each country. The customer does not need to manually select a network.

### Partner Coverage

Roaming partner coverage may differ from the home network. The customer may experience different speeds and quality depending on the roaming partner. Coverage maps for roaming partners are available on the SmartConnect website.

### No Service While Roaming

Verify roaming is enabled on the account. Check that the device has data roaming enabled in settings. Restart the device to force network reselection. If no service persists, manually select a network operator. Contact support if the issue continues.

### Slow Data While Roaming

Roaming speeds may be slower than the home network. This is normal and depends on the roaming partner's network. Try moving to a different location for better signal. Disable background data usage to conserve roaming data. Consider activating an international roaming plan for better speeds.

### High Roaming Charges

If a customer receives unexpected roaming charges: review the customer's roaming usage, check if roaming plans were activated, verify if the usage was domestic or international, and apply credits if appropriate per the billing dispute policy.
# International Roaming Troubleshooting Guide

### Verify Account Status

Confirm the customer's account is in good standing with no past due balance. Verify the line is active and not suspended. Confirm the customer has an active international roaming plan or understands pay-per-use rates.

### Device Preparation

Ensure the device is unlocked if it was purchased with a carrier lock. Verify the device supports the frequency bands used in the destination country. Update device software to the latest version. Back up important data before traveling.

### Settings Configuration

Enable data roaming in device settings. Verify APN settings are correct for international use. Enable Wi-Fi calling as a backup option. Set up the SmartConnect mobile app for account management while abroad.

### Device Cannot Find Network

If the device cannot find any network in the destination country: verify the device is not in airplane mode, check that data roaming is enabled in device settings, restart the device and wait 5 minutes for network search, manually select a network operator in device settings, and verify the destination country is covered by SmartConnect roaming partners.

### Network Registered but No Service

If the device shows a network name but cannot make calls or use data: verify roaming is enabled on the SmartConnect account, check that the international roaming plan is activated, verify the device APN settings are correct, try toggling airplane mode on and off, and contact SmartConnect support for account verification.

### Data Not Working

If data does not work while roaming: verify mobile data is enabled in device settings, confirm data roaming is turned on, check that the roaming plan includes data, verify APN settings are configured for international use, try connecting to Wi-Fi and using the SmartConnect app to troubleshoot, and restart the device after making any setting changes.

### MMS Not Working

MMS may not be available in all roaming destinations. Verify the destination country supports MMS roaming. Check that mobile data is working. Verify MMS APN settings are correct. Some roaming partners do not support MMS, which is a known limitation.

### Unexpected Charges

If a customer receives unexpected charges: review the detailed usage in the SmartConnect app or portal, verify the roaming plan was activated before travel, check if the usage was domestic or international roaming, review the per-use rates for the destination country, and initiate a billing dispute if the charges are incorrect.

### SIM Card Issues While Abroad

If the SIM card is not recognized: remove and reinsert the SIM card, try the SIM in a different device if available, check for physical damage to the SIM card, contact SmartConnect for SIM replacement options while abroad.

### Device Compatibility Issues

If the device does not work on roaming networks: verify the device supports the required frequency bands, check if the device is carrier-locked, confirm the device software is up to date, try a different device if available.

### Emergency Calls

Emergency calls (911, 112, 999) can be made even without roaming activation. The device will connect to any available network for emergency calls. Emergency calls may be routed to the nearest emergency center regardless of the network used.

### Emergency Contacts

If a customer needs emergency assistance while abroad: they can call SmartConnect customer service from any phone, they can visit a SmartConnect partner store in the destination country, they can use the SmartConnect app over Wi-Fi for support, and the emergency support line is available 24/7.
# Device Compatibility Guide

### LTE Bands

SmartConnect uses the following LTE bands. Devices must support at least one band for basic service. Devices supporting multiple bands will have better coverage and performance. Required bands for full LTE experience: Band 2 (1900 MHz), Band 4 (1700/2100 MHz), Band 12 (700 MHz), and Band 66 (1700/2100 MHz).

### 5G Bands

For 5G NR service, devices must support 5G NR bands. Supported 5G bands include: n41 (2500 MHz) for mid-band 5G, n71 (600 MHz) for low-band 5G, and n260 (39 GHz) for mmWave 5G. 5G service requires a 5G-capable device and 5G plan.

### VoLTE Requirements

For voice service, devices must support Voice over LTE (VoLTE). All smartphones sold by SmartConnect are VoLTE capable. BYOD devices must be VoLTE compatible. Devices without VoLTE will not be able to make or receive calls on the SmartConnect network.

### Compatibility Checker

Customers can check device compatibility on the SmartConnect website. The checker uses the device IMEI to verify band support. Customers should check compatibility before purchasing a device for use on SmartConnect.

### IMEI Requirements

The device IMEI must not be blacklisted. The IMEI must be registered with the GSMA database. Devices reported as lost or stolen will not be activated. Customers can check IMEI status on the SmartConnect website.

### Device Unlocking

Devices purchased from other carriers may need to be unlocked. SmartConnect will unlock devices that are fully paid off and not reported as lost or stolen. The unlocking process takes 2-5 business days. Customers can request unlocking through customer service.

### New Device Setup

When setting up a new device on SmartConnect: insert the SIM card or activate eSIM, follow the device setup wizard, connect to Wi-Fi for initial updates, configure APN settings if data does not work, and test voice, data, and messaging.

### eSIM Setup

For devices with eSIM support: scan the QR code provided by SmartConnect, follow the on-screen prompts to activate the eSIM, verify the eSIM is active in device settings, and remove the physical SIM if replacing.

### Data Transfer

When transferring from an old device to a new device: back up data from the old device, restore data on the new device, verify all apps and data transferred correctly, and test all services on the new device.

### iPhone Issues

Some older iPhone models may have VoLTE compatibility issues. Ensure the device is running the latest iOS version. If VoLTE does not work, try toggling VoLTE off and on in Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > Voice & Data.

### Android Issues

Some Android devices may require manual APN configuration. If data does not work, verify APN settings match the SmartConnect defaults. Some Samsung devices have a separate APN for T-Mobile roaming, which may conflict with SmartConnect settings.

### Pixel Issues

Google Pixel devices generally work well with SmartConnect. Ensure the device is running the latest Android version. If VoWiFi does not work, check that the device software is up to date.

### Battery Health

SmartConnect recommends keeping device battery above 20% for optimal performance. Extreme temperatures can affect battery life. Avoid charging the device in direct sunlight or extreme cold.

### Software Updates

Keep device software up to date for best performance and security. Software updates may include carrier settings updates that improve network performance. SmartConnect recommends enabling automatic software updates.
# SIM Card Management Guide

### Physical SIM (nano-SIM)

Standard nano-SIM card for most smartphones. Provides voice, data, and messaging service. The SIM card is tied to the customer's account and phone number. Physical SIMs can be swapped between compatible devices.

### eSIM (embedded SIM)

Software-based SIM built into newer devices. No physical card required. Can be activated remotely by scanning a QR code. Supports multiple lines on a single device. eSIMs are more secure and cannot be physically removed.

### Micro-SIM and Standard SIM

Older SIM card formats that are no longer supported by current SmartConnect plans. Customers with these SIMs should upgrade to a nano-SIM or eSIM. SmartConnect provides free SIM upgrades upon request.

### New Line Activation

A new SIM card is generated and assigned to the customer's account. The SIM is provisioned with the customer's phone number, plan, and service features. The SIM is shipped to the customer or provided at a retail location. Activation occurs when the SIM is inserted into a compatible device.

### Replacement SIM

If a SIM card is lost, damaged, or malfunctioning, a replacement can be issued. The replacement SIM is assigned the same phone number and plan. The old SIM is deactivated immediately upon replacement. The customer must verify their identity before a replacement is issued.

### SIM Swap

A SIM swap transfers the customer's phone number and plan to a new SIM. This is different from a replacement, as it may involve a different SIM type. SIM swaps require identity verification. The old SIM is deactivated immediately.

### SIM Not Recognized

If the device does not recognize the SIM card: remove and reinsert the SIM card, clean the SIM card contacts with a soft cloth, try the SIM in a different device, check for physical damage to the SIM card, and contact SmartConnect for a replacement if the SIM is damaged.

### SIM Locked (PUK Code)

If the SIM is locked due to incorrect PIN entry: the PUK code is printed on the SIM card packaging, enter the PUK code when prompted on the device, set a new PIN after unlocking, and if the PUK code is lost, contact SmartConnect for assistance.

### SIM Not Activated

If a new or replacement SIM is not activating: verify the SIM has been provisioned in the SmartConnect system, insert the SIM into a compatible device and connect to Wi-Fi, wait 15 minutes for activation to complete, and contact SmartConnect if activation fails after 30 minutes.

### SIM Cloning Protection

SmartConnect uses advanced encryption to prevent SIM cloning. If a SIM is suspected to be cloned, contact SmartConnect immediately. The compromised SIM will be deactivated and a replacement issued.

### SIM Lock

SIM lock prevents the use of a stolen SIM card. If a device is reported lost or stolen, the SIM is automatically locked. The customer must contact SmartConnect to unlock or replace the SIM. A locked SIM cannot make calls, send texts, or use data.

### PUK Code Security

The PUK code should be kept in a safe place. If the PUK code is entered incorrectly 10 times, the SIM is permanently locked. A permanently locked SIM requires replacement. The PUK code cannot be reset by the customer.
# Device Financing Program
SmartConnect offers device financing to allow customers to purchase new devices with monthly installments instead of paying the full retail price upfront.

### Payment Structure

The device cost is divided into equal monthly installments over 24 or 36 months. The installment amount is based on the device retail price and the financing term. There is no interest charged on the financing. The total cost equals the retail price of the device.

### Eligibility

Customers must have an active SmartConnect account in good standing. The account must not have any past due balance. The customer must pass a credit check for financing amounts above $500. New customers may be required to make a down payment.

### Credit Check

A soft credit check is performed for financing amounts up to $500. A hard credit check is performed for financing amounts above $500. The credit check does not affect the customer's credit score for soft checks. Customers who do not qualify for financing may pay the full retail price or make a down payment.

### Terms and Conditions

The financing agreement is a separate contract from the service agreement. The agreement specifies the device model, retail price, installment amount, financing term, and payment due date. The agreement also specifies early termination and default provisions.

### Monthly Charges

The device installment is added to the customer's monthly service bill. The installment is a separate line item from the service charges. The installment is due on the same date as the service charges. Late payments on the installment follow the same late payment policy as service charges.

### Ownership

The customer does not own the device until all installments are paid. SmartConnect retains ownership of the device until the financing is complete. The customer is responsible for the device's care and condition. The device may not be sold or transferred while under financing.

### Full Payoff

Customers can pay off the remaining balance at any time. The payoff amount is the total of all remaining installments. No additional fees or penalties apply for early payoff. After payoff, the customer owns the device outright.

### Partial Payoff

Customers can make additional payments toward the device balance at any time. Additional payments are applied to the remaining balance. The monthly installment amount does not change with additional payments. The number of remaining installments is reduced.

### Return Policy

Customers can return a financed device within 14 days of purchase. The device must be in good condition with no damage. The customer receives a refund of all installments paid minus any usage charges. The financing agreement is canceled upon return.

### Device Exchange

Customers can exchange a financed device for a different model within 30 days. The original device must be returned in good condition. The financing is transferred to the new device. Any price difference is adjusted in the monthly installment.

### Trade-In Program

Customers with a financed device can trade in for a new device. The trade-in value is applied to the new device purchase. The remaining balance on the old device is paid off from the trade-in value. Any remaining balance on the old device is added to the new financing.

### Default

A financing agreement is in default if: the customer's service is suspended for non-payment, the customer fails to make payments for 60 days, or the customer breaches the financing agreement terms. Default triggers the remaining balance becoming immediately due.

### Collections

If the financing balance remains unpaid after default, the account may be sent to collections. The customer is notified before the account is sent to collections. Collections activity may affect the customer's credit score. The customer can contact SmartConnect to arrange payment before the account is sent to collections.

### Optional Coverage

SmartConnect offers optional device insurance through a third-party provider. The insurance covers accidental damage, theft, and mechanical failure after the manufacturer warranty expires. The insurance premium is added to the monthly bill. Claims are processed through the third-party provider.

### Insurance Claims

Customers can file insurance claims through the SmartConnect app or website. A deductible applies for each claim. Approved claims result in a replacement device being shipped to the customer. Unauthorized repairs may void the insurance coverage.

# Ticket Management Procedures

### Creation

Tickets are created when a customer contacts SmartConnect with an issue. Tickets can be created via phone, chat, email, or self-service. Each ticket is assigned a unique ticket number. The ticket includes the customer's information, issue description, and initial assessment.

### Assignment

Tickets are automatically assigned to the appropriate team based on category and priority. If a specific agent is available, the ticket is assigned to that agent. If no agent is available, the ticket enters the queue for the next available agent. Customers can request a specific agent for follow-up.

### Investigation

The assigned agent investigates the issue. This may involve reviewing account information, checking network status, running diagnostics, or consulting knowledge base articles. The agent documents all findings in the ticket. If the issue requires additional expertise, the ticket is escalated.

### Resolution

Once the issue is resolved, the agent documents the resolution in the ticket. The customer is notified of the resolution. The customer confirms the issue is resolved. If the customer does not confirm within 48 hours, the ticket is automatically closed with a note that the customer did not confirm.

### Closure

Tickets are closed after the customer confirms resolution or after 48 hours without customer response. Closed tickets are archived for future reference. Customers can reopen a closed ticket within 30 days if the issue recurs.

### Critical (P1)

Service completely unavailable. Affects business operations. No workaround available. Requires immediate attention. Response within 15 minutes. Resolution within 4 hours.

### High (P2)

Service significantly degraded. Major feature unavailable. Workaround may be available. Requires urgent attention. Response within 30 minutes. Resolution within 8 hours.

### Medium (P3)

Service partially affected. Minor feature unavailable. Workaround available. Requires attention. Response within 2 hours. Resolution within 24 hours.

### Low (P4)

Cosmetic issue. Enhancement request. Informational inquiry. Requires response. Response within 8 hours. Resolution within 72 hours.

### Technical Support

Issues related to service functionality. Includes connectivity problems, device issues, and network problems. Assigned to the technical support team.

### Billing Support

Issues related to charges, payments, and account balance. Includes disputes, payment processing, and plan changes. Assigned to the billing support team.

### Account Management

Issues related to account setup, changes, and inquiries. Includes activation, cancellation, and account updates. Assigned to the account management team.

### Sales

New service inquiries, plan recommendations, and device purchases. Assigned to the sales team.

### Customer Updates

Customers are notified of ticket status changes via their preferred communication method. Updates include assignment, investigation progress, escalation, and resolution. Customers can request updates at any time by contacting support.

### Internal Notes

Agents add internal notes to document investigation findings and actions taken. Internal notes are not visible to the customer. Notes are used for continuity when tickets are escalated or reassigned.

### Resolution Documentation

The resolution must be documented clearly in the ticket. Include the root cause, steps taken to resolve, and any preventive measures. Documentation is used for knowledge base updates and training.
# Account Security Procedures

### Verification Methods

Customer identity must be verified before any account changes. Verification methods include: account PIN, last four digits of SSN, security question answers, email verification, and SMS verification code. Multiple methods may be required for high-risk changes.

### High-Risk Changes

The following changes require enhanced verification: account PIN change, authorized user addition or removal, plan change, device upgrade, port-out request, and account closure. Enhanced verification requires two or more verification methods.

### Verification Failure

If identity verification fails, the request is denied. The customer is advised to contact SmartConnect through an alternative channel. Account lockout occurs after 3 failed verification attempts. The customer must visit a retail location with photo ID to unlock.

### PIN Requirements

The account PIN is a 4-6 digit numeric code. The PIN is required for account changes and support interactions. The PIN should not be easily guessable. The PIN should be different from the device unlock PIN.

### PIN Management

Customers set their PIN during account creation. The PIN can be changed through the customer portal, mobile app, or by contacting customer service. The PIN is not visible to SmartConnect employees. The PIN is stored securely and cannot be recovered, only reset.

### PIN Reset

If a customer forgets their PIN, they can reset it through the customer portal using email or SMS verification. If the customer cannot access the portal, they must visit a retail location with photo ID. A temporary PIN is generated and must be changed on first use.

### Suspicious Activity Detection

SmartConnect monitors accounts for suspicious activity. Indicators include: unusual login locations, rapid account changes, multiple failed verification attempts, and unusual usage patterns. Suspicious activity triggers account security alerts.

### Account Lock

If suspicious activity is detected, the account may be temporarily locked. The customer is notified via all registered contact methods. The customer must verify their identity to unlock the account. For high-risk situations, the customer must visit a retail location.

### Recovery

If an account is compromised, SmartConnect works with the customer to secure the account. This may include: resetting all passwords and PINs, reviewing recent account changes, reverting unauthorized changes, and enabling additional security features. The customer is monitored for 30 days after recovery.

### Device Lock

Customers should enable device lock with a PIN, password, or biometric authentication. Device lock prevents unauthorized access if the device is lost or stolen. SmartConnect recommends using at least a 6-digit PIN or alphanumeric password.

### Remote Lock and Wipe

If a device is lost or stolen, the customer can remotely lock or wipe the device. Remote lock and wipe are available through the customer portal or mobile app. Remote wipe erases all data on the device. The device cannot be used after a remote wipe without the account credentials.

### Find My Device

SmartConnect supports the Find My Device feature for compatible devices. Find My Device allows the customer to locate, lock, or wipe the device remotely. The feature requires the device to be powered on and connected to a network. Find My Device is available through the customer portal and mobile app.

### Customer Data Protection

SmartConnect protects customer data in accordance with applicable privacy laws. Customer data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Access to customer data is logged and monitored. Customer data is not shared with third parties without customer consent.

### Data Retention

Customer data is retained for the duration of the service relationship. Account data is retained for 7 years after account closure. Call recordings are retained for 90 days. Support ticket records are retained for 5 years.

### Data Access Requests

Customers can request access to their personal data through the customer portal. Data access requests are processed within 30 days. Customers can also request deletion of their personal data, subject to legal retention requirements.
# Technical Troubleshooting Guide

### Dropped Calls

If a customer reports dropped calls: check the customer's coverage area and signal strength, verify the serving cell site is operational, check for active network events in the area, review the customer's device and SIM status, and if the issue persists, escalate to network engineering with call logs and location data.

### One-Way Audio

If a customer reports hearing the other party but not being heard (or vice versa): verify both parties have active voice service, check for VoLTE registration issues, review the customer's APN settings, test with a different device if available, and if the issue persists, escalate with the call details and timestamps.

### Cannot Make Calls

If a customer cannot make calls: verify the line is active and not suspended, check for sufficient account balance or plan inclusions, verify the device has cellular service, check if VoLTE is enabled on the device, and test with a different device if available.

### Cannot Receive Calls

If a customer cannot receive calls: verify the line is active, check for call forwarding settings, verify the device is not in airplane mode, check for do-not-disturb settings, and verify the customer's number is correctly provisioned.

### No Data Connection

If a customer has no data: verify mobile data is enabled in device settings, check that data is included in the customer's plan, verify APN settings are correct, check for data throttling due to plan limits, and run a speed test to confirm the issue.

### Slow Data

If a customer reports slow data: check the customer's signal strength and quality, verify the serving site is not congested, check for background app data usage, verify no VPN is active, and test at different times to rule out congestion.

### Intermittent Data

If a customer reports intermittent data: check for frequent handovers between cells, review signal quality variations, check for device power-saving settings that may affect connectivity, and verify the device software is up to date.

### SMS Not Sending

If a customer cannot send SMS: verify the line has SMS capability, check for sufficient balance if prepaid, verify the device has cellular service, check the message center number in device settings, and test with a different device if available.

### MMS Not Sending

If a customer cannot send MMS: verify mobile data is working, check MMS APN settings, verify the messaging app has necessary permissions, check for sufficient storage space, and test with a different device if available.

### Delayed Messages

If messages are delayed: check for network congestion, verify the device has good signal, check for large message sizes that may cause delays, and verify the recipient's network is operational.

### Incorrect Charges

If a customer disputes a charge: review the invoice details, check for any promotions or credits that should be applied, verify the plan pricing is correct, and apply credits or adjustments as appropriate per the billing dispute policy.

### Payment Issues

If a customer has payment issues: verify the payment method is valid, check for sufficient funds, review the payment history, and assist with alternative payment methods if needed.

### Plan Change Issues

If a customer has issues with a plan change: verify the change was processed correctly, check the effective date, verify any prorated charges are correct, and assist with any additional changes needed.
# Customer Retention Guide
This document describes the strategies and procedures for retaining customers who are considering leaving SmartConnect.

When a customer requests to cancel service: the cancellation request triggers a retention workflow. The representative must attempt to understand the reason for cancellation. ### Competitive Offers

Customers who mention competitive offers should be flagged for retention. The representative should highlight SmartConnect's differentiators and value. Retention offers may be available to match competitive pricing.

### Service Resolution

The most effective retention strategy is resolving the customer's issue. If the customer is leaving due to a service problem, focus on resolving the problem. Document the issue thoroughly and follow up to ensure resolution.

### Plan Optimization

Review the customer's current plan and usage to identify optimization opportunities. The customer may be on a plan that does not match their needs. Offering a better-fitting plan can improve satisfaction and reduce cost.

Long-term customers may be eligible for loyalty rewards. Loyalty rewards include plan discounts, free add-ons, and priority support. Loyalty rewards are available for customers with 2+ years of continuous service.

Retention offers may include bill credits, plan discounts, or device offers. Retention offers are tiered based on customer value and tenure. Higher-value customers receive more generous retention offers. All retention offers must be approved by a supervisor.

Customers spending more than $100 per month or with 3+ years of tenure. Retention offers include up to 20% plan discount for 6 months, free premium add-ons for 3 months, and waived device upgrade fees. These offers require supervisor approval.

### Medium-Value Customers

Customers spending $50-$100 per month or with 1-3 years of tenure. Retention offers include up to 10% plan discount for 3 months and free standard add-ons for 1 month. These offers require representative approval.

Before processing a cancellation, make one final attempt to retain the customer. Summarize the value the customer receives from SmartConnect. Highlight any loyalty rewards or tenure benefits that would be lost. Offer the best available retention incentive.

After cancellation: send a confirmation email with the cancellation details. Include information about any final charges or credits. Provide information about how to reactivate service if the customer changes their mind. Note the cancellation reason for analytics purposes.

Former customers who canceled within the last 90 days are eligible for the win-back program. The win-back offer is communicated via email and SMS. Win-back offers include enhanced plan pricing and waived activation fees.
